Team — I've reviewed the redlines. Summary of legal position and recommended edits: 

1) SLA exceptions: Quantaflow's proposed SLA carve (removing uptime credit triggers below 99.5%) is a material concession. We should push back; instead propose an interim SLA floor tied to the new incremental capacity only (i.e., baseline SLA unchanged for existing committed volume).

2) Data retention: customer wants a 12-month log/usage retention commitment that expands our standard 90-day analytics retention. We can agree to provide 12-month retention for aggregated usage metrics only, not raw request logs. Any request for raw logs or expanded retention must go through a scoped DPA amendment and potentially additional security review.

3) Term/rollback: their requested immediate termination right for incremental capacity (with 10-day notice) conflicts with our minimum activation/proration terms. Recommend we keep a 30-day removal notice for the incremental capacity and allow pro-rated refunds subject to minimum utilization thresholds.

4) Clause edits: I've added tracked changes to the Order Form doc (Quantaflow_OF_v1-Redlines.docx). Please review the consolidated redline in the deal page before sending to the customer. I flagged one item that may need leadership sign-off (a temporary price below our guardrail for large-volume pilots).

Action items: Jordan to confirm the economic guardrail for the temporary price; Jasmine to confirm whether the 7/22 signature deadline is firm. I'll stand by to finalize the change order text once economics are confirmed.

-Markus
Deputy GC, Redwood Inference
